newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Death toll in Russia station blast rises to three.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Russia station blast rises to three.

text.p: The death toll from a powerful blast at a southern Russian railway station rose to three on Thursday and eight people were still in hospital with injuries, a local Interior Ministry spokesman said.
"Two women and a boy have died as a result of the blast," he told Reuters by telephone from the city of Krasnodar.
The explosive device, which went off in the town of Armavir on Wednesday evening, had been concealed in wrapping paper and left under a bench in the station waiting room, he said.
No one has claimed responsibility but the spokesman said police were searching for three suspects, including two men apparently from the Caucasus region.
Armavir is about 320 km (200 miles) from the separatist region of Chechnya, and the railway line goes to the Chechen capital Grozny.

Radical separatist rebels in Chechnya have threatened to stage attacks on Russian cities to commemorate the anniversary of independence leader Dzhokhar Dudayev's death in a Russian rocket attack on April 21 last year.

But Chechen vice-president Vakha Arsanov, who is standing in for President Aslan Maskhadov while he is away on a Moslem pilgrimage, denied any Chechen involvement in the incident and blamed it on Russian special security forces.

Tass quoted Arsanov late on Wednesday as denying that the "Chechen resistance forces" had carried out the blast. Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev told Tass he was ready to help Russian security forces solve the case.

Separatist rebels staged two bloody hostage-taking raids outside Chechnya during their almost 21-month conflict with Russia. A ceasefire was agreed last August but talks bogged down over the region's demands for complete independence.
